title: Compulsory waiting period before promotion - is it legally valid
p1:
A promotion can be delayed even when an employee is fully eligible.

But can an organisation legally force someone to wait before moving up?
p2:
Many believe that once an employee meets the eligibility criteria, promotion becomes an automatic right. That is not always true.

A compulsory waiting period, often called a minimum qualifying service period, may be valid if it is created through proper rules and applies fairly to everyone.
p3:
The key point is that employers or authorities usually have the power to set reasonable conditions for promotion, such as experience requirements, performance standards, or a required period in a particular role.

However, an arbitrary delay without a valid rule can be challenged because promotion policies must follow fairness and non-discrimination principles.

A waiting period is not automatically illegal. Its validity depends on the rules behind it, how it is applied, and whether it serves a legitimate purpose.
conclusion: Have you seen a promotion being delayed because of a compulsory waiting period? Do you think such rules ensure fairness or create unnecessary barriers?
